# DATA-2 results — generated by `run_spc.py`, not hand-edited

## 1. Control-chart constants, derived vs published

`d2` is computed by numerically integrating the expected range of *n* standard normals; `c4` from log-gamma. The published column is Montgomery, *Introduction to Statistical Quality Control*, Appendix VI. If these disagreed, every limit in the platform would be wrong by a constant and no test downstream would notice.

| n | d2 derived | d2 published | abs err | c4 | A2 derived | A2 published | abs err |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 1.12838 | 1.128 | 3.79e-04 | 0.7979 | 1.8800 | 1.880 | 2.88e-05 |
| 3 | 1.69257 | 1.693 | 4.31e-04 | 0.8862 | 1.0233 | 1.023 | 3.27e-04 |
| 4 | 2.05875 | 2.059 | 2.49e-04 | 0.9213 | 0.7286 | 0.729 | 4.03e-04 |
| 5 | 2.32593 | 2.326 | 7.11e-05 | 0.9400 | 0.5768 | 0.577 | 1.81e-04 |
| 6 | 2.53441 | 2.534 | 4.13e-04 | 0.9515 | 0.4832 | 0.483 | 2.46e-04 |
| 7 | 2.70436 | 2.704 | 3.57e-04 | 0.9594 | 0.4193 | 0.419 | 2.84e-04 |
| 8 | 2.84720 | 2.847 | 2.01e-04 | 0.9650 | 0.3725 | 0.373 | 4.73e-04 |
| 9 | 2.97003 | 2.970 | 2.63e-05 | 0.9693 | 0.3367 | 0.337 | 3.03e-04 |
| 10 | 3.07751 | 3.078 | 4.95e-04 | 0.9727 | 0.3083 | 0.308 | 2.64e-04 |

Worst absolute disagreement on d2: 4.95e-04 — i.e. the published table rounded to three decimals.

## 2. Within-subgroup limits vs the overall-sigma mistake

| characteristic | correct limit width | naive limit width | ratio | disturbances detected (correct) | detected (naive) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| shaft_dia_mm | 0.0260 | 0.0775 | 2.99x | 3/3 | 2/3 |
| wall_thk_mm | 0.0531 | 0.1693 | 3.19x | 2/2 | 2/2 |
| cavity_mix_mm | 0.0746 | 0.1565 | 2.10x | 1/1 | 1/1 |
| seal_force_N | 15.3236 | 36.4573 | 2.38x | 0/0 | 0/0 |
| bore_rough_um | 0.2302 | 0.5253 | 2.28x | 0/0 | 0/0 |

The ratio column is the whole argument. Overall sigma contains the very between-subgroup variation the chart exists to detect, so a disturbed process widens its own limits and then looks calm inside them. Note the direction of the effect: it is worst exactly when the process is worst.

## 3. Per-rule economics: what each rule costs and what it buys

Probability the rule fires at least once over a 200-point chart. The left column is the false-alarm rate on a perfectly in-control process; the right is the detection rate when the process has shifted 1σ. Both matter — a rule with high power and high false-alarm rate is how charts get ignored.

| rule | description | P(fires) in control | P(fires) at 1σ shift |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 point beyond 3 sigma (WE) | 42.0% | 99.2% |
| 2 | 2 of 3 consecutive points beyond 2 sigma, same side (WE) | 33.1% | 100.0% |
| 3 | 4 of 5 consecutive points beyond 1 sigma, same side (WE) | 49.5% | 100.0% |
| 4 | 8 consecutive points on one side of the centre line (WE) | 54.0% | 100.0% |
| 5 | 6 consecutive points steadily increasing or decreasing (Nelson) | 6.4% | 6.4% |
| 6 | 14 consecutive points alternating up and down (Nelson) | 17.8% | 17.8% |
| 7 | 15 consecutive points within 1 sigma, either side (Nelson: stratification) | 17.4% | 0.2% |
| 8 | 8 consecutive points beyond 1 sigma, either side (Nelson: mixture) | 1.4% | 41.3% |
| 1-8 stacked | all eight rules together | 93.6% | 100.0% |
| 1-4 stacked | classic Western Electric only | 89.3% | 100.0% |

**Stacking inflation, measured.** Rule 1 alone fires on 42.0% of clean 200-point charts. The four classic Western Electric rules together: 89.3%. All eight: 93.6% — a 2.2× increase in nuisance alarms over rule 1 alone. Every rule is another test on the same data. Shops that enable all eight because the software offers them are buying sensitivity with a currency they have not been shown the price of.

## 4. ARL: the head-to-head, at matched false-alarm budgets

EWMA (λ=0.2) is used at **L = 2.861**, not the textbook 2.962. At the textbook value this implementation measures ARL₀ = 487, because it uses exact time-varying limits rather than the asymptotic ones the published constants assume. Calibrated, ARL₀ = 366. CUSUM (k=0.5) at h = 4.781 gives ARL₀ = 376. Comparing detectors at different ARL₀ is how any chart can be made to win.

| shift | Shewhart (rule 1) | Shewhart (WE 1-4) | Shewhart (all 8) | EWMA | CUSUM |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.0σ | 374.2 | 92.3 | 77.2 | 366.3 | 376.4 |
| 0.5σ | 156.8 | 27.7 | 26.9 | 35.0 | 35.6 |
| 1.0σ | 43.2 | 9.4 | 9.4 | 8.7 | 9.8 |
| 1.5σ | 14.8 | 5.1 | 5.1 | 4.3 | 5.5 |
| 2.0σ | 6.2 | 3.4 | 3.4 | 2.7 | 3.8 |
| 3.0σ | 2.0 | 1.8 | 1.8 | 1.5 | 2.5 |

Row 1 is the false-alarm budget: rule 1 alone measures ARL₀ = 374 against the theoretical 370.4, while the same chart with all eight rules enabled measures 77 — the stacking cost again, now in run-length units.

At a 1σ shift, EWMA signals in 8.7 points and CUSUM in 9.8, against 43.2 for a 3σ Shewhart chart. So why not EWMA everywhere? Look at the 3σ row: Shewhart needs 2.0 points, EWMA 1.5. The memory that makes EWMA sensitive to small shifts also makes it *slower* on large ones, because the shifted observation is averaged with in-control history. Add that an operator can read a Shewhart chart without explaining what a smoothing constant is, and the answer is tool-per-purpose: Shewhart for the floor, EWMA/CUSUM alongside it for the slow drifts the floor chart will not catch.

## 5. Capability, and the refusals

| characteristic | verdict | Cp | Cpk | Pp | Ppk | method |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| shaft_dia_mm | **REFUSED** (2 OOC points) | — | — | — | — | — |
| wall_thk_mm | computed | 1.01 | 1.01 | 1.03 | 1.03 | normal |
| cavity_mix_mm | **REFUSED** (45 OOC points) | — | — | — | — | — |
| seal_force_N | **REFUSED** (4 OOC points) | — | — | — | — | — |
| bore_rough_um | computed | 0.78 | 0.78 | 0.77 | 0.76 | normal |

A refusal is a feature. `capability.assess()` raises `NotInControl` rather than returning a number with a footnote, because Cpk converts a mean and a sigma into a tail probability, and an unstable process has neither. The footnote gets deleted on the way to the customer; the number does not.

### What the refusal protects against

Numbers a tool without the gate would have printed:

| characteristic | Cpk | Ppk | Cpk/Ppk | predicted PPM | observed PPM |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| shaft_dia_mm | 1.54 | 1.15 | 1.34 | 277 | 0 |
| wall_thk_mm | 1.01 | 0.71 | 1.43 | 33,442 | 43,200 |
| cavity_mix_mm | 0.67 | 0.71 | 0.94 | 23,359 | 5,000 |
| seal_force_N | 1.17 | 1.10 | 1.06 | 510 | 6,000 |
| bore_rough_um | 0.78 | 0.76 | 1.02 | 22,353 | 19,000 |

The Cpk/Ppk column is the diagnostic. A ratio near 1 means the process is not moving: short-term and long-term spread agree. A large ratio means the process is capable within a subgroup and is not staying put between them — and the action that follows is completely different. Chasing spread on a drifting process is how improvement budgets get spent on the wrong thing.

## 6. Gauge R&R — is it the process or the instrument?

ANOVA method, 10 parts × 3 operators × 3 repeats, crossed. AIAG MSA-4 bands.

| study | %GRR of total variation | ndc | repeatability (EV) | reproducibility (AV) | interaction kept | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| good_gauge | 4.6% | 30.6 | 0.0353 | 0.0249 | yes | **acceptable** |
| marginal_gauge | 16.0% | 8.7 | 0.1272 | 0.0874 | yes | **conditional** |
| bad_gauge | 37.9% | 3.4 | 0.3179 | 0.2373 | yes | **UNACCEPTABLE** |
| bore_rough_um_study | 82.7% | 1.0 | 0.0530 | 0.0329 | yes | **UNACCEPTABLE** |

**The misdiagnosis case.** `bore_rough_um` has σ_process = 0.040 µm and σ_gauge = 0.075 µm — the instrument is noisier than the thing it measures. Its gauge study returns %GRR = 82.7% and ndc = 1.0: the measurement system can distinguish roughly 1 category of part. Any capability study on this characteristic is measuring the gauge. Any improvement project chartered off its control chart is chartered against noise. ndc is the number to put in front of a manager: not a percentage, but *how many different sizes of part this instrument can actually tell apart*.
